ranking.note: Keeps P2 but moves to the front: it introduces the BlockTemplateManager that #33922, #36356/#36357 and #36469 build on, plus a real latency/lock-contention win.
Raised from 10th: it is the only user-visible defect here (miners get a false 'Internal bug detected' on longpoll during shutdown, issue #34262), so it leads the P3 block.
Placed ahead of #36357 because that PR is based on it; reviewing out of order wastes effort.
Kept P3 but last in band: category guidance ranks changes worth a tiny fraction of a block's fees low, and this only recovers exact-limit underfill.
Lowered to P4: reviewers confirm the no-mempool lookup path is unreachable in production, making this a narrow contract-consistency fix rather than a real bug fix.

inconsistencies: Chain: #36356 (move getblocktemplate cache into BlockTemplateManager) must be reviewed before #36357 (move BlockAssembler statics), which is explicitly based on it; both in turn presume the BlockTemplateManager introduced by #35581.

#35581 is a prerequisite for #33922 (reference-counted template memory in BlockTemplateManager) and for the #36356/#36357 refactors and #36469's shared validation-state catcher; it cannot be reviewed after them.
#35598 was extracted from #33922 and exercises the same waitNext/feeThreshold behaviour; review the standalone test first so #33922 does not carry it.

#36192 and #35598 are both mining-IPC functional test additions touching interface_ipc_mining.py and the regtest constants; merge order matters only for conflicts, not priority, but a single reviewer can take them together.
#36356/#36357 and #36469 all touch BlockTemplateManager internals; #36469 deduplicates helpers that #35581/#36356 introduce, so it should come last of the refactor set.

#36367 is scoped as mempool prioritisetransaction clamping; its stated mining impact (getblocktemplate dropping prioritised txs via FeeFrac overflow) is the only reason it sits in this category, and the triggering deltas are unrealistic.
result.notes: No P1 here: nothing on the list risks producing an invalid block or an immediate fund-safety failure. The P2 group is the external-miner interface work (template manager, TxCollection, memory load, precious submission) that Stratum v2 consumers depend on; the P3 group is a mix of a genuine shutdown bug, scoped-state refactors tied to the BlockTemplateManager project, and test coverage; P4 is pure internal cleanup plus one unreachable-path consistency fix.
